public_rationale: On the stated reading of proof as credible financial evidence, the categorical assertion fails. Before the post, document-based reporting put OpenAI's 2025 adjusted gross margin at a positive 33%. Anthropic reporting also described a positive projected margin, though that projection is not decisive. Whole-company losses do not establish losses on inference. This assessment does not establish net profitability or a fully audited inference margin.
limitations: The result depends on accepting financial-document reporting as proof.
The decisive figure is an adjusted gross margin; its complete cost reconciliation was not accessible.
The original reporting was inaccessible through read_page, so a readable news report was used.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is no proof any AI lab is profitable on inference and plenty of evidence they are not.

statement.excerpt: I must be abundantly clear that nobody has any proof that anyone is profitable on inference, but we have plenty of proof they’re not.

our_interpretation: Read profitability on inference as revenue exceeding the costs of serving models, before training and other company expenses.
Read proof as credible financial evidence, including reporting based on financial documents, rather than requiring publicly audited accounts.

Use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual period discussed in the surrounding financial claims. Evidence must also have been public before the post to contradict the assertion about what evidence existed.
criteria.support_condition: Public financial evidence establishes negative inference margins across the relevant labs, without credible evidence of a positive margin.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible financial reporting available before the post establishes a positive inference-related gross margin for at least one lab.

evidence.explanation: Reporting attributed to internal financial documents describes a positive adjusted gross margin despite rising inference costs. It supplies evidence against the categorical assertion under the stated gross-margin reading, while leaving the adjustments incompletely documented.
This reports a positive projected margin after inference and selling costs. A projection is not a realized result, so it is not independently decisive.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A public reconciliation of realized serving revenue, all inference costs, and adjustments would remove the remaining measurement uncertainty.
